nodes.description: Public mapping (address => uint256) recording each investor's balance; read in profit calculation and updated with msg.value in the fallback.
Public mapping (address => uint256) recording the block number of the sender's last transaction; used in the profit subtraction and updated at the end of the fallback.
Public address of the casino/house; set once in the constructor from msg.sender and used as the recipient of the 5% tip transfer.
Constructor executed at deployment; assigns house = msg.sender, giving the deployer the privileged tip-receiving role.

Unnamed external payable fallback function handling all incoming transactions: computes profit, performs a pseudo-random coin toss, transfers ether to the caller and to the house, then updates balance and atBlock.
Caller-controlled address used as the mapping key for balance/atBlock and as the recipient of the payout transfer.
Block timestamp used as input to blockhash() in the pseudo-random toss generation; miner-influenceable randomness source.
Unchecked arithmetic expression balance[msg.sender] * 5 / 100 * (block.number - atBlock[msg.sender]) / 5900, susceptible to overflow/underflow (Solidity 0.4.24 has no built-in checks).
External call msg.sender.transfer(profit * 2) executed before balance and atBlock are updated, enabling reentrancy into the fallback.
External call house.transfer(winning * 5 / 100) executed before state is reconciled, a second external-call point inside the unprotected fallback.
Unchecked state update balance[msg.sender] += msg.value performed after the external transfers, vulnerable to arithmetic overflow and reentrancy-driven state inconsistency.
Local uint256 holding the computed 5%-per-day profit derived from balance, block.number and atBlock.
Local uint8 holding the coin-toss outcome derived from keccak256 over blockhash(block.timestamp), block.difficulty and block.coinbase.
Local uint256 holding the doubled profit amount sent to the caller and used to compute the house tip.

edges.reason: msg.sender is used as the key to read balance[msg.sender] when checking whether the caller has an active investment.
msg.sender indexes atBlock[msg.sender] to obtain the caller's last transaction block.
Any external caller (msg.sender) can invoke the payable fallback by sending a transaction to the contract.
The caller-controlled address msg.sender is the recipient of the external transfer performed before state updates, exposing the fallback to reentrancy.
block.timestamp flows into blockhash() inside the keccak256 toss computation, making the lottery outcome predictable/manipulable by miners (timestamp dependency).
balance[msg.sender] is multiplied by 5/100 inside the unchecked profit expression, permitting overflow of the intermediate product.
atBlock[msg.sender] is subtracted from block.number inside the unchecked profit expression, permitting underflow.
The result of the unchecked arithmetic operation is stored in the local variable profit, carrying any overflow/underflow forward.
profit is doubled and passed to msg.sender.transfer, the external call that can re-enter the fallback before balance/atBlock are written.
The local profit value is multiplied by 2 to produce the winning amount held in the local variable winning.
winning flows into house.transfer(winning * 5 / 100), a second external call executed prior to state reconciliation.
msg.sender keys the unchecked balance[msg.sender] += msg.value update, which can overflow the stored balance.
The fallback branches into msg.sender.transfer when the toss is zero, and state is not updated until after the call returns.
The fallback always executes the unchecked balance[msg.sender] += msg.value statement after the conditional payout logic.
The constructor assigns house from msg.sender, granting the deployer the privileged position of tip recipient.
The pseudo-random toss value determines whether the payout branch (msg.sender.transfer) is taken.
The toss outcome controls entry into the block that also executes the house.transfer tip.

normalization_plan.reason: The temporary local profit only exists to carry the result of the unchecked arithmetic expression; it should be folded into that unsafe arithmetic operation.
The local toss value is a transient randomness result used solely for branch selection inside the fallback function and has no independent identity.
The local winning value is only computed to feed the house.transfer tip call, so it should be merged into that unsafe external-call operation.
